title: Which Is Faster: Electricity or the Electrons?
description:
The lamp turns on almost instantly, but individual electrons drift surprisingly slowly.

The electromagnetic signal propagates through the circuit very quickly, while electron drift speed in a conductor is usually much slower.

The electric field establishes along the circuit and nearby electrons respond; energy transfer is not one electron travelling from switch to bulb.

The electrons already present throughout the wire begin moving together when the circuit is completed.
